lines: The podcast explores how the modern internet evolved from the mid-1990s to the iPhone era, highlighting that many failed dot-com ventures merely lacked infrastructure and market maturity rather than sound concepts.
Host and guest note that major tech shifts typically start with hobbyists working on long-term horizons driven by passion rather than quarterly profit pressures.
Companies like eBay pioneered trust mechanisms such as reputation systems, proving that faceless strangers could safely transact in a digital economy.
Google achieved dominance by integrating a relevance-based ad model that created a win-win ecosystem for users, advertisers, and the platform.
Napster proved that instant convenience drives media consumption, a lesson the music industry initially missed by focusing strictly on piracy laws.
title: Replay: How the Internet Happened | Chris Dixon & Brian McCullough (2018)
